decisions.reason: The cited complex chain rule requires scalar maps between open subsets of C, whereas projective transitions for n>1 have vector domains and codomains. The original Definition also left vector-valued holomorphy unspecified. Repaired by defining the complex-linear first-order criterion, computing the ratio-transition expansion, and proving surface-map chart independence with the scalar quotient rule; the one-variable chain rule now applies only to source-coordinate changes.

F14 incorrectly required every isolated-singularity principal part to be finite. The actual supplier allows infinitely many negative Laurent powers; exp(1/z) is a counterexample to the old sentence. Only meromorphic coefficients occur in steps2.2-3.1, so their principal parts are finite and the residue proof is unaffected. F14 now states the general definition and restricts finiteness to these meromorphic differentials.

reviews.reason: The ratio expansion has complex-linear term h_l/a_k-a_l h_k/a_k^2 and remainder O(||h||^2) at a_k nonzero, including the omitted numerator a_j=1,h_j=0. Finite componentwise convergence gives precisely ordinary holomorphy for maps from a surface. Scalar quotient rules handle target changes; the scalar chain rule handles source changes. Quotient charts, projection-matrix separation, sphere-surjection compactness, countable bases, smooth rational transitions, nonvanishing paths and projective linear actions remain valid. No choice principle or new item is needed. Owning manifest and boundary contract were synchronized.

Read the Statement, all four proof steps and actual direct supplier interfaces. The local products mu_i=eta_i times evaluation(s_D,omega) are meromorphic, have holomorphic differences, and agree in principal parts. Their globally compatible pole set is locally finite and hence finite on compact X. The smooth splitting u_i has delta u=delta mu and the supplied normalized comparison gives dbar u_i. Off the poles dbar u_i=-dbar mu; the clockwise deleted boundaries supply the second minus sign, giving the positive residue sum. Exact-form integrals vanish and bounded smooth corrections vanish on shrinking circles; P empty and zero forms are included. Full AC and supplied metrics/good cover remain as stated. Only F14 changed; the Statement is byte-identical. The F14 contract now additionally quotes the actual meromorphic-differential supplier; strict checks pass for both assigned items.
